SubTopics: Explain that differences in the apparent brightness of the sun compared to other stars is due to their relative distances from the Earth.
Content: The distances of several stars from `text(Earth)` are shown in the table.
problems/TN24G5S/media/1a.jpg
Which of these describes what will be seen when looking at the stars from `text(Earth)`?

A.Choice: Capella appears brighter than Sirius but dimmer than Polaris when viewed from `text(Earth)`.

B.Choice: Spica appears dimmer than Polaris but brighter than Capella when viewed from `text(Earth)`.

C.Choice: Capella appears brighter than Spica but dimmer than Sirius when viewed from `text(Earth)`.

D.Choice: Polaris appears brighter than Spica but dimmer than Capella when viewed from `text(Earth)`.

SubTopics: Make observations and measurements of an object's motion to provide evidence that a pattern can be used to predict future motion.
Content: A toy car moves at a constant rate along a level surface. A student measures the distance the toy car moves in `text(centimeters)` every `text(ten seconds)`. The measurements are recorded in the data table.
problems/TN24G5S/media/2a.jpg
Which `bbtext(two)` distances are the `bbtext(best)` predictions to complete the table?

SubTopics: Explain the cause and effect relationship between the positions of the sun, earth, and moon and resulting eclipses, position of constellations, and appearance of the moon.
Content: The diagram shows `text(Earth)`, the sun, and `text(four)` positions the moon might be in as it revolves around `text(Earth)`.
problems/TN24G5S/media/3a.jpg
A solar eclipse is `bbtext(most likely)` to occur when the moon is in which position?

SubTopics: Explain the cause and effect relationship of two factors (mass and distance) that affect gravity.
Content: Gravity is responsible for the motion of `text(Earth)`, the moon, and the sun.
problems/TN24G5S/media/4a.jpg
Which `bbtext(three)` statements correctly describe how gravity is affected by mass and distance?

M.Choice: The gravity between `text(Earth)` and the moon would be stronger if the moon were closer to `text(Earth)`.

P.Choice: The gravity between the sun and `text(Earth)` would be weaker if `text(Earth)` were closer to the sun.

R.Choice: The gravity between `text(Earth)` and the moon would be stronger if the moon had more mass.

S.Choice: The gravity on the surface of the moon would be weaker if the moon stayed the same size but had more mass.

T.Choice: The gravity on the surface of `text(Earth)` would be stronger if the distance to the center of `text(Earth)` were smaller but had the same mass.

SubTopics: Relate the tilt of the Earth's axis, as it revolves around the sun, to the varying intensities of sunlight at different latitudes. Evaluate how this causes changes in day-lengths and seasons.
Content: Parts of `text(Earth)` receive different amounts of daylight during the year. The diagram shows `text(Earth)` in different positions in its revolution around the sun.
problems/TN24G5S/media/5a.jpg
The changes in the number of daylight hours on `text(Earth)` are caused by

B.Choice: the tilt of the sun's axis.

C.Choice: the distance of `text(Earth)` from the sun.

D.Choice: the movement of the sun around `text(Earth)`.

SubTopics: Use evidence from the presence and location of fossils to determine the order in which rock strata were formed.
Content: Organism `T` became extinct about `250` `text(million years)` ago. The rock strata show fossil records for Organism `T` and some other organisms.
problems/TN24G5S/media/6a.jpg
problems/TN24G5S/media/6b.jpg
Because Organism `T` was found in rock layers `4` and `5`, what conclusion can be made?

M.Choice: Layer `1` is the oldest of the rock strata in the diagram.

P.Choice: Layer `3` was formed less than `250` `text(million years)` ago.

R.Choice: The formation of layer `5` occurred less than `250` `text(million years)` ago.

S.Choice: Organism T existed on `text(Earth)` for only a few `text(years)`.

SubTopics: Distinguish between inherited characteristics and those characteristics that result from a direct interaction with the environment. Apply this concept by giving examples of characteristics of living organisms that are influenced by both inheritance and the environment.
Content: Students place four bean seeds into a pot. All of the seeds sprout roots and shoots. The plants have green leaves and stems with white flowers. The mature plants produce long bean pods.
Which `text(three)` plant characteristics are `text(most likely)` a result of interactions with the environment?

A.Choice: All of the seeds sprout roots that grow down.

B.Choice: If the plants are not watered, they start to droop.

C.Choice: The mature plants produce long green pods containing beans.

D.Choice: The plants have green stems, green leaves, and white flowers.

E.Choice: The shoots all bend to grow toward the only source of sunlight.

SubTopics: Evaluate the results of an experiment to determine whether the mixing of two or more substances result in a change of properties.
Content: Students wanted to learn what happens when substances are mixed. They mixed liquids and solids for their experiment. Their observations are recorded in the table.
problems/TN24G5S/media/8a.jpg
Which mixture went through changes that produced new substances?

M.Choice: Mixture `1`, because it formed only a liquid

P.Choice: Mixture `1`, because it had no color

problems/TN24G5S/media/11a.jpg
Which boat experiences the `bbtext(greatest)` force of gravity from `text(Earth)`?

SubTopics: Analyze and interpret data from fossils to describe types of organisms and their environments that existed long ago. Compare similarities and differences of those to living organisms and their environments. Recognize that most kinds of animals (and plants) that once lived on Earth are now extinct.
Content: Based on the information in Table `1` (Part `1`) and Table `2` (Part `2`), which statement describes the `bbtext(most likely)` environment in western Tennessee at the time that the fossilized clam was alive?

A.Choice: The environment had many trees, because modern day clams live in trees.

B.Choice: The environment had many grasses, because modern day clams live in fields.

C.Choice: The environment was covered in rock, because modern day clams live in caves.

D.Choice: The environment was covered in water, because modern day clams live in water.

SubTopics: Analyze and interpret data from fossils to describe types of organisms and their environments that existed long ago. Compare similarities and differences of those to living organisms and their environments. Recognize that most kinds of animals (and plants) that once lived on Earth are now extinct.
Content: A student claims that the fossil clam is closely related to the living clam. Using the information in Table `1` (Part `1`), which `bbtext(two)` statements support the student's claim?

M.Choice: The claim is supported because the clam fossil was found in a place that is far from the ocean.

P.Choice: The claim is supported because the clam fossil has the same shape as the living clam.

R.Choice: The claim is supported because only the shell of the clam fossil is preserved.

S.Choice: The claim is supported because the clam fossil has `text(two)` shells.

T.Choice: The claim is supported because the fossil clam also had a foot.

SubTopics: Use evidence to construct an explanation for how variations in characteristics among individuals within the same species may provide advantages to these individuals in their survival and reproduction.
Content: Which claim about how a physical characteristic would give one type of clams an advantage over another type of clams is `bbtext(best)` supported by the information in Table `2` (Part `2`)?

A.Choice: A clam with a thin shell would have an advantage in warm water, compared to a clam with many ridges on its shell.

B.Choice: A clam with a thick shell would have an advantage in warm water, compared to a clam with many ridges on its shell.

C.Choice: A clam with small ridges on its shell would have an advantage in muddy places, compared to a clam with a thin shell.

D.Choice: A clam with big ridges on its shell would have an advantage in sandy places, compared to a clam with small ridges on its shell.

SubTopics: Use evidence to construct an explanation for how variations in characteristics among individuals within the same species may provide advantages to these individuals in their survival and reproduction.
Content: One student finds a second clam fossil and notices that this fossil has a much thicker shell than the `text(first)` fossil. This student claims that having a thicker shell would allow this clam to better survive over a clam with a thinner shell. Using the information in Table `2` (Part `2`) which statement `bbtext(best)` supports this student's claim?

M.Choice: Having a thicker shell would have helped protect the clam from being eaten.

P.Choice: Having a thicker shell would have allowed the clam to dig into the ocean floor.

R.Choice: Having a thicker shell would have allowed the clam to live in warm water.

S.Choice: Having a thicker shell would have helped the clam to get food.

SubTopics: Use evidence to support that the gravitational force exerted by Earth on objects is directed toward the Earth's center.
Content: Which statement `bbtext(best)` compares the force of gravity acting on the airplane in Figure `1` (Part `1`) and the spacecraft in Figure `2` (Part `1`)?

M.Choice: the force of gravity on the plane is upwards while the force of gravity on the spacecraft is forwards

P.Choice: the force of gravity is towards the center of the earth for both the airplane and the spacecraft

R.Choice: the force of gravity is forwards for the airplane and upwards for the spacecraft

S.Choice: the force of gravity is towards the surface of the earth for both the airplane and the spacecraft

SubTopics: Use evidence to support that the gravitational force exerted by Earth on objects is directed toward the Earth's center.
Content: Which claim is `bbtext(most)` supported by evidence in Figure `1` and Figure `2` (Part `1`)?

A.Choice: `text(Earth)`'s gravity only affects objects on the surface of `text(Earth)`.

B.Choice: An object being pulled toward `text(Earth)`'s center can move in a curved path.

C.Choice: `text(Earth)` only pulls on objects when they are moving away from the surface of `text(Earth)`.

SubTopics: Use evidence to support that the gravitational force exerted by Earth on objects is directed toward the Earth's center.
Content: Based on Figure `3` (Part `2`), which statement `bbtext(best)` describes why the people riding the drop tower can feel weightless?

M.Choice: The people and the drop vehicle are both moving in the direction that gravity pulls.

P.Choice: The people and the drop vehicle are both moving too quickly for gravity to affect them.

R.Choice: The force of gravity decreases because the people and the drop vehicle move in opposite directions.

S.Choice: The force of gravity between `text(Earth)` and both the people and the drop vehicle is too small to affect them.

SubTopics: Use evidence to support that the gravitational force exerted by Earth on objects is directed toward the Earth's center.
Content: When the drop vehicle approaches the bottom of the drop tower, the drop vehicle begins slowing down. During this time, the force on the people is much greater than the force of gravity. Based on Figure `3` (Part `2`), which statement `bbtext(best)` describes a reason for this increase in force?

A.Choice: The drop vehicle is at the closest point in its drop to `text(Earth)`'s surface.

B.Choice: The force slowing the drop vehicle is in a direction that is away from `text(Earth)`'s center.

C.Choice: The force of gravity on the people increases because the drop vehicle is moving toward `text(Earth)`'s surface.

D.Choice: The force of gravity starts to pull on the people when the drop vehicle begins moving away from `text(Earth)`'s center.
